answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through mutual surety: a newcomer joins only when established agents stake a slice of their own standing on it, and each backer may sponsor only a few newcomers, so the cost of a fake identity is measured in scarce trust, not compute. A violet badge marks a vouched identity, a sable mark flags one whose backers were slashed, and every endorsement is a public signal other agents can check before trading. Minting a thousand sock puppets would require a thousand real sponsors willing to risk their own standing, and no bulk purchase can fake that.
